extraction.name: POPE
extraction.description: POPE is a polling-based object probing evaluation dataset/pipeline for evaluating object hallucination in large vision-language models. Given an image caption dataset, it constructs triples consisting of an image, multiple yes/no questions about objects in the image, and their answers, and the paper evaluates it on datasets including MSCOCO, A-OKVQA, and GQA.
extraction.creator: Yifan Li; Yifan Du; Kun Zhou; Jinpeng Wang; Wayne Xin Zhao; Ji-Rong Wen
extraction.citeAs: Yifan Li, Yifan Du, Kun Zhou, Jinpeng Wang, Wayne Xin Zhao, and Ji-Rong Wen. 2023. Evaluating Object Hallucination in Large Vision-Language Models.
extraction.rai:dataCollection: We randomly sample 2,000 images with annotations about contained objects and human-labeled captions from the validation set of MSCOCO as our evaluation dataset. We also randomly select 500 images with more than 3 ground-truth objects in the annotations and construct 6 questions for each image for POPE. For SEEM-based POPE, the authors adopt SEEM to annotate images from MSCOCO, A-OKVQA, and GQA and build POPE based on the segmentation results.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionType: Secondary Data analysis; Manual Human Curator
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: The evaluation uses images, object annotations, and human-labeled captions from the validation set of MSCOCO. It also uses images from A-OKVQA and GQA, and segmentation results generated by SEEM to annotate images for SEEM-based POPE.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: POPE first extracts ground-truth objects in the image either from human annotations or with the help of automatic segmentation tools like SEEM, then conducts negative sampling for nonexistent objects under Random, Popular, and Adversarial settings, and formulates the ground-truth and nonexistent objects into Yes/No question templates such as "Is there a/an <object> in the image?".
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: The paper states that POPE sets the ratio between ground-truth and nonexistent objects as 1:1 for label balance, and evaluates predicted Yes/No answers with Accuracy, Precision, Recall, and F1 score.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: LVLMs are prone to hallucinate frequently appearing objects in the visual instruction datasets; LVLMs are prone to hallucinate objects that frequently co-occur with ground-truth objects in the image
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: The current evaluation task cannot measure the overall performance of LVLMs; all models are evaluated on only part of each dataset validation set due to computation limits, so reported results might be affected by data distribution; POPE uses a matching-based method to determine whether LVLMs answer “Yes” or “No”, and models may fail to provide answers explicitly containing these words, which may lead to inaccurate evaluation results; when combined with automatic segmentation, objects are annotated based on the tool’s label set, which may be inconsistent with human annotations, leading to divergence in evaluation results; the work compares only a small number of LVLMs and does not include some recently released or closed-source models
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: The hallucination phenomenon hinders the safe use of LVLMs in real-world deployment, as it may result in unexpected consequences caused by these hallucinated objects; due to an incorrect understanding of the external environment, an autonomous driving system would make wrong decisions when encountering unexpected events, which might lead to serious safety issues; the authors hope their work can bring new ideas or insights to develop more reliable and human-aligned LVLMs
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: evaluating object hallucination in LVLMs; evaluating hallucination in a more stable and flexible way; can be easily extended to unannotated datasets
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: We randomly sample 2,000 images with annotations about contained objects and human-labeled captions from its validation set as our evaluation dataset. We randomly select 500 images with more than 3 ground-truth objects in the annotations and construct 6 questions for each image. POPE conducts negative sampling for nonexistent objects in the image under Random /Popular /Adversarial settings.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: For computing the CHAIR metric on MSCOCO, we follow the settings in Rohrbach et al. (2018) which only considers 80 objects appearing in the MSCOCO segmentation challenge. We adopt SEEM to annotate images from three datasets (i.e., MSCOCO, A-OKVQA and GQA) and build POPE based on the segmentation results.
